title: Resilient Typed-Output Orchestration Experiment
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Objective: validate an orchestration strategy and test harness that enables graceful recovery when typed/JSON-mode responses deviate under streaming + tool-calling workloads. Focus on scenarios where partial streams, interleaved tool invocations, and model-side schema-skew occur simultaneously. Deliverables: reproducible simulation harness, metric dashboard, automated regression for CI, and a recommended fallback policy for production runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce 5 canonical failure modes (truncated json, extra-unexpected-fields, missing-required-field, mis-typed-field, interleaved toolcall fragment)
Automated runs produce actionable metrics: schema_violation_rate, median_recovery_latency_ms, successful_reassembly_rate
A runtime policy (config + patch) that reduces customer-visible schema errors by >= 60% under mixed workloads in the staging cluster
CI job added that fails the build on >1% regression in schema_violation_rate across canonical prompts
test_plan: 1) Create synthetic workload generator that mixes: short-form completions, long streaming responses, and tool-calls (up to 2 nested tool calls per request). 2) Inject controlled perturbations from model variants: random key order, extra punctuation, unexpected tokens between json fields, and truncated suffixes. 3) Run 10k requests per variant across t2/t4-like latency profiles, collect telem and parse outcomes. 4) Validate decoder behavior: constrained-decoder vs permissive-decoder, compare fallback strategies: graceful-retry, sanitizer-pass, speculative-parse+repair.
scenarios: Partial-stream where closing brace arrives >3000ms after last token (stream gap)
Interleaved tool call fragments: model emits toolcall JSON, then resumes with extraneous narrative text
Model emits numeric field as string and sometimes as null (type-flapping)
Unexpected additional top-level field that downstream consumers ignore vs strict reject
Prefix-cached KV replay combined with schema drift (old prefix expects v1 schema, model returns v2)
implementation_notes: - Implement harness as a standalone Go runner + Python scenario definitions so infra team can run in CI. - Use existing telemetry hooks (trace IDs) and add a lightweight schema-flight-recorder that logs raw token streams for failed parses. - Keep sanitizer rules pluggable: allow route-level config to prefer permissive parse vs strict enforcement. - No DB schema changes.
risks: If sanitizer logic is too permissive we could mask regressions and surface downstream data quality issues.
High flakiness in synthetic perturbations may make CI thresholds brittle; need calibration with traffic shaping.
Runtime CPU overhead for repair strategies may increase p50 latency under heavy burst workloads.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and DX teams. Agreed to prototype harness in a new repo under ri-sim.
2026-02-20: Prototype generator merged - can produce interleaved toolcall sequences and stream gaps. Basic parser counts produced.
2026-02-27: First experimental run in staging (5k requests) comparing constrained-decoder and permissive-decoder. Observed 7.8% baseline schema_violation_rate on v2 model variant.

2026-03-03: Design decision: implement speculative-parse+repair as primary fallback, sanitizer-pass as secondary. Rationale: speculative-parse fixes ~40% of truncated-stream cases without retrying upstream.
2026-03-06: PR opened for schema-flight-recorder (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127. Waiting on security review for PII retention policy.

2026-03-10: Interim results after adding KV-prefix awareness: schema_violation_rate dropped to 2.9% in staged run with repair policy enabled. Noted CPU increase ~12% at 95th percentile under synthetic bursts.
Next: Run extended 50k-request sweep across hardware profiles, log regressions, and propose config defaults for hosted API routes. Coordinate with release owners for runtime-1.28 rollout window.
next_steps: Complete large-scale runs (50k requests) across t2/t4-like clusters by 2026-03-17
Add CI gating job and baseline artifact upload to artifacts storage
Tune repair heuristics to cap CPU overhead under the 8% threshold or add opt-in runtime flag
Draft runtime config patch for default fallback policy and route-level overrides
